title: Structured Output Sunset Safeguards and Migration Checklist
creator: Aisha B. Thompson
description: Prepare a cautious, observable deprecation path for legacy structured-output behaviors and related tool/function-calling edge cases. Provide a prescriptive migration checklist for customers and internal SDKs, plus a test suite to validate backward compatibility during toggles and staged rollouts.
background: Recent rollout of stricter structured-output parsing in api-2026.01 exposed discrepancies in how tool-calling tokens and streaming heuristics are handled by older clients. Several enterprise customers rely on legacy behavior flags. We need an explicit sunset plan that minimizes customer disruption while enabling cleanup of behavior flags and simplification of the runtime.
proposal_summary: Introduce a three-stage sunset: (1) deprecation announcement + compatibility flags for 6 months, (2) opt-in strict mode behind a flag and migration helpers in SDKs, (3) removal of legacy flag with automated compatibility probes and customer-facing migration dashboards. Instrument runtime to emit a structured 'compatibility_score' metric per request to monitor regressions.
migration_checklist: Inventory clients calling structured_output + tool calls and tag by SDK version and language
Publish migration guide with code snippets for preferred SDKs (Python/Node/Go) showing explicit model parameters to preserve legacy behavior
Add a CLI 'redwood-migrate-structured-output' tool for customers to run test prompts against their suite
Ship SDK helpers: enableLegacyStructuredOutput(true) and validateStructuredSchema(schema) with warnings
Provide a compatibility shim server that translates legacy streaming framing into new framing for a 90-day bridge
Create a customer communication plan with target segments (P0 enterprise customers first)
compatibility_tests: Round-trip test: client prompt -> hosted instrumented runtime -> client parser; assert identical output and tokenization for 99.9% of prompts
Tool-call firing test: ensure function call detection triggers identical call payloads under legacy flag and strict mode
Streaming chunk boundary tests covering partial JSON objects and tool-call markers
Load regression test: validate tail-latency and token-cost delta across flag states using production traffic replay
Fuzz tests for structured-output parsers (generate malformed payloads, confirm graceful degradation)
rollout_plan: Week 0: Publish deprecation RFC and migration guide; enable telemetry for compatibility_score
Week 1-4: Offer opt-in strict mode behind behavior flag; gather telemetry and customer feedback
Week 5-12: Coordinate SDK releases with migration helpers and the compatibility shim; onboard top 20 customers to run CLI migration tool
Week 13-20: Begin automated compatibility probes against customer-provided prompt suites (opt-out available)
Week 24: Target removal of legacy flag for new tenants; announced 30-day notice before complete removal for existing tenants
decision_log: 2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting — agreed on three-stage sunset and the need for an SDK migration helper (notes: drive/link-designdoc-123)
2026-02-28: PM/Eng sync — decided to emit compatibility_score metric and a new request header 'X-StructCompat-Version' for tracing
2026-03-03: Design review — UX for migration dashboard approved (design PR: https://drive.redwood/designs/structured-output-migration-v1)
2026-03-08: Engineering trade-off — compatibility shim to be implemented as opt-in gateway to avoid extra runtime costs for all tenants (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-shim/pull/42)
2026-03-11: Legal & Security review — decided no additional encryption changes required; document retention policy updated
acceptance_criteria: Published migration guide and CLI tool with examples for Python and Node
SDK helper functions merged and released in Python/Node/Go
Compatibility test suite green on CI and runbook defined for failures
Telemetry (compatibility_score + X-StructCompat-Version) visible in Console dashboards
Top 10 enterprise customers have completed migration trials or opted into shim
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unanticipated parser behavior in third-party clients — Mitigation: provide compatibility shim and CLI validator
Risk: Increase in support load during opt-in period — Mitigation: dedicate a 2-week triage rotation and provide runbooks to Customer Success
Risk: Runtime cost for dual-path handling — Mitigation: make shim opt-in and limit default runtime branching; monitor cost metrics and throttle probes
